{{Short description|Topological duality}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Lefschetz duality''' is a version of [[Poincaré duality]] in [[geometric topology]], applying to a [[manifold with boundary]]. Such a formulation was introduced by {{harvs|txt|author-link=Solomon Lefschetz|first=Solomon|last=Lefschetz|year=1926}}, at the same time introducing [[relative homology]], for application to the [[Lefschetz fixed-point theorem]].<ref>Biographical Memoirs By National Research Council Staff (1992), p. 297.</ref> There are now numerous formulations of Lefschetz duality or '''Poincaré–Lefschetz duality''', or '''Alexander–Lefschetz duality'''.

==Formulations==
Let ''M'' be an [[orientable]] [[compact space|compact]] [[manifold]] of dimension ''n'', with boundary <math>\partial(M)</math>, and let <math>z\in H_n(M,\partial(M); \Z)</math> be the [[fundamental class]] of the manifold ''M''. Then [[cap product]] with ''z'' (or its dual class in cohomology) induces a pairing of the (co)[[homology group]]s of ''M'' and the relative (co)homology of the pair <math>(M,\partial(M))</math>. Furthermore, this gives rise to isomorphisms of <math>H^k(M,\partial(M); \Z)</math> with <math>H_{n-k}(M; \Z)</math>, and of <math>H_k(M,\partial(M); \Z)</math> with <math>H^{n-k}(M; \Z)</math> for all <math>k</math>.<ref>{{cite book|first=James W.|last= Vick|title=Homology Theory: An Introduction to Algebraic Topology|year=1994|page=171}}</ref>

Here <math>\partial(M)</math> can in fact be empty, so Poincaré duality appears as a special case of Lefschetz duality.

There is a version for triples.  Let <math>\partial(M)</math> decompose into subspaces ''A'' and ''B'', themselves compact orientable manifolds with common boundary ''Z'', which is the intersection of ''A'' and ''B''. Then, for each <math>k</math>, there is an isomorphism<ref>{{cite book|last=Hatcher|first= Allen|author-link=Allen Hatcher|url= https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html |title=Algebraic topology|publisher= [[Cambridge University Press]]|location=Cambridge| year=2002|isbn=0-521-79160-X|page=254}}</ref>

:<math>D_M\colon H^k(M,A; \Z)\to H_{n-k}(M,B; \Z).</math>
